statement: Theodore Komnenos Doukas of Epirus captured the Latin Kingdom of Thessalonica (1224) — a Crusader state established for Boniface of Montferrat after 1204 — in a major westward expansion of Epirote power. The capture made Theodore the most powerful Greek ruler of the moment; he proclaimed himself Emperor of the Romans in 1224, the first claimant to challenge Nicaea's imperial monopoly. The capture of Thessalonica, however, led to overextension: Theodore's subsequent advance was halted by Bulgarian Tsar Ivan Asen II at the Battle of Klokotnitsa (1230), where Theodore was captured and blinded.
